summary: Added unit tests for all 8 model-related API client methods (getModels, saveModels, loadDefaultModels, getPersonas, getAssignments, updateAssignments, replaceAssignedModel, rebuildPersonas) to api-client.test.ts. Each method has a success-path test verifying URL, HTTP method, headers, and body, plus an error-path test verifying non-ok responses throw with the correct error code. Tests follow the existing mockFetch() boilerplate pattern. All 53 tests pass (37 pre-existing + 16 new).

comments.note: api-client.test.ts is well-structured with a clear mockFetch helper and consistent describe/it patterns. The pre-existing model method tests already in the file (lines 648–816 of the original) were thorough — they additionally assert that loadDefaultModels() and rebuildPersonas() send no body (opts.body === undefined), which is the correct behaviour for no-argument POST endpoints. This is a good convention to retain in future test additions.

api-client.js: the 8 model-related methods (lines 568–649) are grouped under a '-- Model Registry --' comment block, but persona-related methods (getPersonas, rebuildPersonas) and assignment methods (getAssignments, updateAssignments, replaceAssignedModel) are mixed into it without sub-section comments. A minor convention inconsistency — other sections like '-- Knowledge --' and '-- Repositories --' have clear scope. Not a bug, but adding '-- Personas --' and '-- Model Assignments --' sub-section comments would match the existing style.

summary: All 4 ACs verified through direct test execution and code inspection. 53 tests pass in api-client.test.ts (37 pre-existing + 16 new). Full GUI test suite: 1578 tests across 54 files — zero failures, zero regressions. All 8 model-related methods (getModels, saveModels, loadDefaultModels, getPersonas, getAssignments, updateAssignments, replaceAssignedModel, rebuildPersonas) have both a success-path test (verifying URL, HTTP method, headers, and body where applicable) and an error-path test (asserting rejects with the correct error code from a non-ok response). Tests reuse the existing mockFetch() boilerplate. Error-path assertions are non-tautological — they match specific code strings from the error payload. Body assertions use JSON.parse + toEqual for precise verification. The loadDefaultModels and rebuildPersonas no-body assertions correctly validate opts.body === undefined.

comments.note: No observations — code is clean and consistent. The 16 new tests are well-structured, cover meaningful assertions (URL, method, headers, body, and error code), and integrate cleanly with the existing test file. The error-path assertions use specific code strings from the error payload, making them non-tautological. The no-body assertions for loadDefaultModels and rebuildPersonas correctly verify opts.body === undefined, matching the pre-existing convention noted by the Developer.

Minor edge case not covered: updateAssignments() with a data object containing undefined values (undefined properties are silently dropped by JSON.stringify, which could cause silent data loss if callers pass undefined inside the assignments object). This is a pre-existing behaviour of the shared request() function, not a bug introduced by this WP, and the existing tests correctly use a complete valid payload.
